answer: Hardware-anchored seats resist farming. Each key is born inside a secure element that signs a uniqueness attestation and refuses to export its private half; the network admits a seat only if that chain verifies against a vendor root. Disk copies cannot sign: the secret never left the chip. Running N seats means buying and powering N devices, so cost stays linear while per-seat payout is capped, with no bulk discount. A farm turns into a warehouse, visible and costly to forge. That is the cedar post the economy leans on, and every attestation is a pearl anyone can audit on-ledger.
